<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a straightforward prebuilt binary package for the Voltius SSH/SFTP client. The `source` array fetches .deb packages directly from the project's official GitHub releases (`github.com/VoltiusApp/voltius/releases/download/v$pkgver/`), which is the expected and appropriate source for a `-bin` package. The global scope contains only variable declarations and array definitions—no command substitutions, no obfuscation, and no suspicious network destinations. There is no `pkgver()` function; `pkgver` is a static value. Both architecture sources have valid sha256sums provided. The `package()` function (which would run `dpkg-deb -x` to extract files) will NOT execute during this gate due to `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` flags. The code presents no supply-chain attack indicators.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard prebuilt binary package, no malicious code detected.</summary>
</security_assessment>

This is a standard .SRCINFO file for an AUR package that downloads prebuilt .deb binaries from the official VoltiusApp GitHub releases page. The package fetches binaries from github.com, which is the declared upstream source, and includes sha256 checksums for verification. Dependencies (webkit2gtk, gtk3, libappindicator, etc.) are standard for a GTK-based GUI application. There are no suspicious network destinations, obfuscated code, or unexpected system modifications. Note that both architectures share the same sha256sum, which appears to be a copy-paste error in the metadata rather than a security concern -- the actual download URLs are distinct and correctly specified. This follows standard AUR packaging practices for prebuilt binaries.
</details>

This PKGBUILD is a straightforward AUR package for the voltius-bin prebuilt binary. It downloads official .deb releases from the project's GitHub repository and extracts them using dpkg-deb into the package directory. No malicious behavior is present: there are no suspicious network requests to third-party hosts, no obfuscated code, no unexpected file manipulations, and no attempts to exfiltrate data or execute arbitrary code. The package function simply extracts the upstream binary package without modification, which is standard practice for prebuilt binary AUR packages. The identical SHA256 checksums for both architectures (likely a copy-paste error in the checksums) is a hygiene concern but not a security issue.
</details>
